poll-order.why: PriorityQueue is a min-heap by default: each poll removes the smallest remaining element.

max-heap.why: Comparator.reverseOrder() turns it into a max-heap: poll removes 9, and the largest left is 3.

top-k-cost.why: Each of the n numbers costs at most one insert and one removal on a heap of size k, O(log k) each.

top-k-heap.why: The question you ask on each new number is "is it bigger than the smallest of my top k?", and a min-heap answers that with peek and evicts it with poll.

iteration-order.why: The iterator walks the heap's internal array, which is only partially ordered. Only repeated poll() gives priority order.

merge-k.why: The heap picks the next smallest of k heads in O(log k): O(n log k) overall. Sorting everything is O(n log n); scanning all heads every time is O(n·k). A stack can't pick a minimum.
